welcome.name: Welcome — joining an organization
welcome.subject: {{ inviter_name }} added you to {{ organization_name }} on Servantium
welcome.sends: Postmark template `welcome`, transactional. Sent when someone adds a person to an existing organization. It is also the invitation: the new account has no password until they set one.

email.note: The address they'll sign in with

welcome-organization.name: Welcome — new organization
welcome-organization.subject: Your Servantium organization is ready
welcome-organization.sends: Postmark template `welcome-organization`, transactional. Sent to the first administrator when a new organization is created. Like `welcome`, it carries the set-password link.

email.note: The address they'll sign in with

password-reset.name: Password reset
password-reset.subject: Reset your Servantium password
password-reset.sends: Postmark template `password-reset`, transactional, from a backend function that generates the link. Until that exists, Firebase sends it: paste firebase/password-reset.html into Authentication → Templates.

email.note: The account's address. Firebase fills %EMAIL% in its own copy.

reset_url.note: Firebase Admin SDK generatePasswordResetLink(email). Firebase fills %LINK% in its own copy.

task.name: Task message
task.subject: {{ actor_name }} {{ action }}: {{ task_name }}
task.sends: Postmark template `task`, transactional. Sent to the people on a task when something happens to it: it's assigned, someone comments, a date moves, it's completed. One template for every task event — `action` says which.

action.note: Lower-case, reads after the name: assigned you · commented on · changed the due date of · completed

status.note: The task's status as the app shows it

message.example: Please reconcile the Wave 1 manifest against Aurora's forecast before the first PK run. Flag anything outside the 10% tolerance.
message.note: The note or comment that came with the event. Leave it out and the panel doesn't appear.

plan_url.note: Leave it out and the plan link doesn't appear

notification.name: Notification
notification.subject: {{ headline }}
notification.sends: Postmark template `notification`, transactional. The general-purpose notification for everything that isn't a task: approvals, mentions, a quote changing status, a plan being published. One template, many events — the product fills in what happened.

category.note: One or two words for the banner label: Quote · Approval · Mention · Plan

headline.example: Dana Whitfield approved the Phase II quote
headline.note: What happened, in one line. Also the subject.

summary.note: The line that shows after the subject in the inbox

message.example: Version 3 of the quote is approved. The project plan can now be staffed — the roles below are still unassigned.
message.note: One or two sentences of detail

details.note: Rows for the summary table, as { label, value }. At least one.

action_label.note: The button label, 24 characters or fewer

reason.example: Sent because you lead AUR-417 in Halcyon Bioanalytical Services.
reason.note: Why this person got it, one short sentence starting “Sent because…”

digest.name: Digest
digest.subject: {{ summary }}
digest.sends: Postmark template `digest`, transactional. A scheduled job sends it to people who chose a daily or weekly summary instead of an email per event. One email, many updates. Needs notification preferences in the app before it ships.

highlights.example: 2 tasks assigned to you, a quote approved, and 2 more
highlights.note: The line after the subject in the inbox

example.title: Jules Hart assigned you “Clinical sample manifest reconciliation”
Dana Whitfield approved the Phase II quote
Sam Okafor commented on “Method validation report”
example.context: NVX-102 · “Draft is in the shared folder.”

example.title: The plan for NVX-102 was published
Priya Nair added a note to AUR-417

items.note: The updates, newest first, as { category, time, title, context, url }. Ten at most — the rest go in `more`.

more.note: When there are more than ten. Leave it out otherwise.

preferences_url.note: Where they change or stop the digest

support-received.name: Support — request received
support-received.subject: [{{ ticket_id }}] {{ ticket_subject }}
support-received.sends: Postmark template `support-received`, transactional. The automatic first reply when a request reaches help@. Set Reply-To to the request's own address (e.g. help+1042@servantium.com) so replies join the right conversation.

ticket_subject.example: Quote total doesn't match my spreadsheet
ticket_subject.note: The subject as they wrote it

reply_by.note: Our promise, as policy sets it: “within one business day”, “by Tuesday”

support-reply.name: Support — reply in a conversation
support-reply.subject: [{{ ticket_id }}] {{ ticket_subject }}
support-reply.sends: Postmark template `support-reply`, transactional. Every message from our team on a request: answers, questions back, and the resolution. Keep the same subject, set In-Reply-To and References to the previous message's Message-ID, and set Reply-To to the request's own address, so the whole conversation stays in one thread in their inbox and in ours.

agent_name.note: Who on our team wrote this reply

preview.example: Thanks for the screenshots — we've found the cause.

example.text: Thanks for the screenshots — we've found the cause. Totals were rounding each line before adding them up, which is why yours came out $12 higher than your spreadsheet.
We've fixed it for your organization, and the Aurora quote now shows $184,500. Could you check it matches on your side?

reply.note: The new message, one item per paragraph, as { text }. Plain text: split on blank lines.

status_note.example: We'll keep this open until you confirm.
status_note.note: Where things stand, when it helps: “We've marked this resolved. Reply if you need anything else — it reopens automatically.”

example.author: Dana Whitfield
example.excerpt: Here are the screenshots. The quote says $184,512 but my sheet says $184,500 for the same roles and hours.

example.author: Priya Nair
example.excerpt: Thanks, Dana. Could you send a screenshot of the quote and the matching rows of your spreadsheet?

example.author: Dana Whitfield
example.excerpt: The total on the Aurora Phase II quote doesn't match my spreadsheet. Which one is right?

thread.note: Earlier messages, newest first, as { author, time, excerpt }. Excerpt: the message as one paragraph, 300 characters at most.

ticket_subject.example: Quote total doesn't match my spreadsheet

incident.name: Incident — service disruption
incident.subject: Service disruption: {{ incident_title }}
incident.sends: Postmark template `incident`, transactional, to each administrator of an affected organization: when the incident opens and at every status change.

incident_title.example: Quotes and project plans aren't loading

update.example: Some organizations see an error when opening a quote or a project plan. Sign-in and everything else is working. We've found where requests are failing and are working on a fix.

incident-resolved.name: Incident — resolved
incident-resolved.subject: Resolved: {{ incident_title }}
incident-resolved.sends: Postmark template `incident-resolved`, transactional, to everyone who received `incident` for the same incident.

incident_title.example: Quotes and project plans weren't loading

summary.example: A configuration change slowed one of our databases, and requests for quotes and project plans timed out. We rolled the change back and added a check so the same change can't ship again.

maintenance.name: Scheduled maintenance
maintenance.subject: Scheduled maintenance on {{ date }}
maintenance.sends: Postmark template `maintenance`, transactional, to every administrator, at least 72 hours before a planned window.

reason.example: upgrade the database that stores quotes and project plans

affected.example: Everything: the web and mobile apps, and API integrations

release-notes.name: Release notes
release-notes.subject: What's new in Servantium — June 2026
release-notes.sends: Postmark template `release-notes`, broadcast stream. Rewritten each month from the help site’s release notes, then sent to active users in batches of 500. Postmark skips anyone who has unsubscribed.

regulatory-notice.name: Regulatory notice
regulatory-notice.subject: Notice: changes to Servantium's sub-processors, effective {{ effective_date }}
regulatory-notice.sends: Postmark template `regulatory-notice`, transactional, one message per organization administrator. The change itself arrives as data (`change_summary`, `change_details`), so the template stays generic and nothing about an upcoming change is written into this public repo. Replies go to help@, which is monitored — the body invites objections by reply. Legal review pending.

change_summary.example: We're adding a sub-processor to deliver in-app email notifications, such as task assignments and password resets. It will process your users' names and email addresses only. It will not process project, quote or financial data.
change_summary.note: What's changing, in plain words. Written and approved per notice; never stored in this repo.

change_details.note: The facts of the change as { label, value } rows: sub-processor, purpose, data processed, location.
